subject: rc
title: RC.------PROG.CONT.
description: Diagram in SR(TRS)II-18 (Social Reality / Trans-Information, Level Two), second of two on book p162, paired with v2-p162-1. Continues the closing education argument by holding race as concept against progressional-continuance — the question of whether race-thinking can be reconciled with real cultural continuance. (C)RC (the concept of race) is crossed with PROG-CONT (progressional continuance): the question is what race-as-concept produces when crossed with progressional-continuance — under conditions where narrow information lines sustain spectacle. SPT-DY (spectacle dynamics) feeds in from the upper-left. ATTN (attention) sits between subject and partner on the left. PROG-CONT sits at the upper-center. INFO-DY (information dynamics) anchors the upper-right output. RE-ST (restructuralism) sits below the central axis. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) and VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) form the lower-right output cluster. STY (style) hangs on the lower-left margin. INDIV-DY-RT (individual-dynamics reality) anchors the lower-center. IST-PT (interior-source point) anchors the bottom-center. Structural argument: race-as-concept crossed with progressional-continuance is mediated by attention as central hub and restructuralism as lower hub. The doubled lower upstreams — style on one side, individual-dynamics-reality plus interior-source-point on the other — register Braxton's structural commitment that real continuance requires individual-dynamics-reality (the (rt) suffix marks it as real) as the deeper upstream. The diagram exposes Braxton's diagnostic: race-as-concept can productively cross with progressional-continuance only when interior-source-point is the lower foundation — when education works at that level — and only then does the affinity-dynamics/vibrational-dynamics output cluster register cultural transformation.
